_meta.indication: Routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with hemophilia A with FVIII inhibitors or hemophilia B with FIX inhibitors.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-national, multi-center, open-label, randomized-controlled trial; 52 patients previously treated on-demand were randomized 1:2 to no prophylaxis (arm 1) or Alhemo prophylaxis (arm 2), plus two non-randomized Alhemo prophylaxis arms (arms 3 and 4).
pivotal_trials.population: Male patients with hemophilia A or B with inhibitors who have been prescribed, or are in need of, treatment with bypassing agents: 91 adults (58 HAwI and 33 HBwI) and 42 adolescents (22 HAwI and 20 HBwI).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Ratio of annualized bleeding rates (ABR) of treated bleeding episodes between Alhemo prophylaxis (arm 2) and no prophylaxis (arm 1).
pivotal_trials.n: 133 patients treated with Alhemo (randomized arms 1 and 2: 52 patients; arm 1 N=19, arm 2 N=33).
pivotal_trials.result: ABR ratio 0.14 (p<0.001), an 86% reduction in ABR with Alhemo prophylaxis vs no prophylaxis; estimated mean ABR 1.7 (95% CI: 1.01, 2.87) on Alhemo vs 11.8 (95% CI: 7.03, 19.86) on no prophylaxis.

key_safety: Most frequently reported adverse reactions (incidence >=5%) were injection site reactions (18% vs 0%) and urticaria (6% vs 0%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 6.1% of patients (renal infarct and hypersensitivity). Venous and arterial thromboembolic events were reported in 1.3% of patients (4/320).
target_moa: Concizumab-mtci is a monoclonal antibody antagonist of endogenous Tissue Factor Pathway Inhibitor (TFPI); inhibition of TFPI enhances FXa production during the initiation phase of coagulation, improving thrombin generation and clot formation to achieve hemostasis.

rems.type: A REMS is not necessary to ensure the benefits of concizumab outweigh the risks.

companion_dx_detail: Dose optimization requires measuring concizumab-mtci plasma concentration by Concizumab ELISA after 4 weeks; CDER approved without the companion diagnostic and no FDA-authorized test is currently available, with a PMC for development of the companion diagnostic.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened to discuss this application; no issues were identified that would have benefitted from a public discussion with external experts.

requirement.text: 4761-1: Conduct adequate analytical and clinical validation testing to establish an FDA cleared or approved in-vitro diagnostic device to accurately and reliably detect concizumab concentration in human 3.2% citrated plasma that is safe and effective for concizumab dose adjustment decisions 4 weeks after initiation of treatment with concizumab in patients with Hemophilia A and B with inhibitors. The final report should include the results of the validation studies to inform product labeling.
